prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Liberal Democrat Manifesto 2010 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core theme: Fairness. The Lib Dems propose four priorities to “hard‑wire fairness” into British life:
- Fair taxes that put money back in your pocket
- A fair chance for every child
- A fair future by creating green jobs and rebuilding the economy
- A fair deal from politics, restoring trust and civil liberties

Fair taxes and responsible finances
- Raise the income tax personal allowance to £10,000, giving most basic-rate taxpayers a £700 cut and lifting 3.6m out of income tax.
- Pay for it by: aligning capital gains tax with income tax; restricting pension tax relief to the basic rate; tackling avoidance/evasion; switching Air Passenger Duty to a per‑plane duty with higher rates for non‑essential domestic flights; a 1% Mansion Tax on property value above £2m; reforming non-dom status.
- Deficit plan: more than £15bn annual savings identified; timing of cuts based on economic conditions from 2011–12. Savings include scrapping ID cards/biometric passports/ContactPoint/Eurofighter Tranche 3B; bank levy until banks are split; curbing quangos, consultants and central inspection regimes; a £400 cap on annual public sector pay rises for two years; welfare and programme reforms. No like-for-like Trident replacement; establish a cross‑party Council on Financial Stability.

Economy, jobs and green growth
- Break up banks (separate retail/investment), reform bonuses, get lending to viable firms.
- Create a UK Infrastructure Bank to crowd‑in private capital to transport and energy.
- One‑year green stimulus creating ~100,000 jobs: retrofit public buildings; eco cash‑back for home energy upgrades; refurbish shipyards for offshore wind; bus scrappage; bring 250,000 empty homes into use; major youth work placements and skills support.
- Support SMEs: reduce red tape, end “gold‑plating” of EU rules, reform business rates to site value, refocus RDAs, back local enterprise funds and regional stock exchanges, invest in broadband.

Schools, skills and universities
- £2.5bn Pupil Premium to boost funding for disadvantaged pupils; cut class sizes; expand one‑to‑one tuition and catch‑up.
- Free schools to innovate; slimmed-down curriculum and standards body; reform testing and league tables; expand high‑quality vocational routes and college options 14–19.
- Scrap tuition fees over six years (immediately for final-year students); national bursary scheme; more foundation degrees and adult apprenticeships.

Health and care
- Protect front‑line NHS by cutting waste and bureaucracy; halve DH size, scrap Strategic Health Authorities; integrate health and social care; expand mental health access; prioritise dementia research; curb harmful alcohol pricing; improve air quality. More local control via elected health boards and staff budget responsibility.

Families and fairness
- Shared, flexible parental leave; extend right to request flexible working to all; stronger child protection and youth services; equal minimum wage over 16s (except apprentices).
- Pensions: restore earnings link with a “triple lock”; raise tax-free threshold benefits pensioners; scrap compulsory retirement ages; respite breaks for carers; long‑term care commission.

Communities, crime, immigration and housing
- 3,000 more police on the beat; cut police bureaucracy; elected police authorities; focus on rehabilitation, restorative justice, and a presumption against short sentences.
- Immigration: reintroduce exit checks; create a National Border Force; regional points-based system; focus deportations on criminals; earned citizenship for long‑term, law‑abiding residents; fair, independent asylum with right to work; end child detention.
- Housing and transport: bring empty homes into use; national home insulation; more council housing finance freedoms; cut rail fares (RPI‑1% on regulated fares); empower councils on buses; cancel Heathrow third runway; per‑plane duty; prepare fair road pricing.

Environment and global role
- Zero‑carbon Britain by 2050; at least 40% electricity from non‑carbon sources by 2020; major home efficiency programme; reject new nuclear; no unabated coal; build a European Supergrid.
- Meet 0.7% of GNI on aid by 2013; global financial reform; anti‑corruption and tax haven crackdown.
- Defence: strategic review; no like-for-like Trident; better forces’ pay and housing; more EU defence cooperation.
- Europe: pro‑EU reform; in/out referendum on future fundamental change; euro only if conditions/right and via referendum.

Political reform and civil liberties
- Fair votes (STV), cut MPs by ~150, fixed‑term parliaments, fully elected second chamber, recall for corrupt MPs, donation caps, lobbying register, written constitution.
- Freedom Bill: curb surveillance, regulate CCTV, end mass data retention, reduce pre‑charge detention to 14 days, scrap control orders, protect Human Rights Act.
